exposure: first vaginal birth after cesarean section (fVBAC)
cervical dilation at the time of previous cesarean
caesarean section late in labor (≥ 8 cm cervical dilatation)
outcome: Course of labor (duration of 1st and 2nd stages)
Risk of obstetric anal sphincter injury
finding: Compared to primiparous women having a vaginal birth, women having their first vaginal birth after a cesarean section have a shorter 1st stage of labor (particularly if the cesarean was performed in advanced labor), a higher risk of sustaining cervical lacerations and perineal trauma.
mod_finding: This study compared women having their first vaginal birth after cesarean section (VBAC) to women having a primiparous vaginal birth and found that the VBAC group had a shorter first stage of labor, a higher risk of cervical lacerations and perineal trauma, but no difference in the risk of anal sphincter injuries.
